sections.h2: Where is the Newton County Recorder of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds sits in Suite 209 of the courthouse at 101 S Wood St in Neosho, MO 64850, and the phone line is (417) 451-8224. The recorder's own website says the office is on the main floor in the northeast corner of the building. Staffed hours are 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday, with holidays closed.

Timing matters for a closing. The office accepts recordings until 3:30 pm, and anything handed in after that goes onto the books the next business day in the order received. Marriage licenses stop being issued at 3:00 pm. Mail goes to P.O. Box 604, and the email address is recorder@ncrecorder.org.

Jenny Childers holds the office. She began as a deputy recorder in 2000, became chief deputy in 2010 and started her second term as the elected recorder on January 3, 2023.

sections.h2: What does the Newton County recorder keep on file?
sections.html:
The office is the permanent record of who owns land in Newton County. It records warranty deeds, deeds of trust, releases, plats, surveys and powers of attorney, and it also holds military discharges plus state and federal tax liens.

A few limits are worth knowing before you call:

  • Staff cannot practice law, so they will not draft a deed, hand out legal forms or explain what a filed paper means.
  • The office does not produce abstracts of title or opinions on the status of a title (RSMo 59.200.1).
  • A title company or attorney prepares the paper; the recorder indexes it, scans it and keeps the permanent copy.

The land lies here, so the deed goes here. RSMo 442.380 directs any written conveyance of real estate to the recorder of the county where that real estate is situated.

sections.h2: How much does recording a deed cost in Newton County?
sections.html:
The county fee page lists $26 for the first page of a standard document and $3 for each page after that. Because a flat $2.00 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 took effect on August 28, 2026, call (417) 451-8224 for the figure on your invoice today.

The recorder keeps any overpayment of up to $10 so a slightly short or long check does not trigger a rejection, as long as the payment is not below the statutory fee. A document that releases or assigns several items carries $5 for each item past the first.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like before the Newton County recorder accepts it?
sections.html:
The recorder may refuse a paper that breaks the layout rules in RSMo 59.310. The office will record a nonconforming document if you pay the $25 surcharge, but a clean first try is cheaper. The county's format page boils the rules down:

  • Letter-size white or light paper of at least 20 pound weight, no watermarks or logos, printed on one side only
  • Black or dark ink, type of at least 8 point, signatures with the name typed or printed beneath
  • A blank three-inch strip at the top of page one for the recorder's stamp, and margins of at least three-quarters of an inch elsewhere
  • Below that strip on page one: the title, the date, every grantor with marital status, every grantee, any statutory addresses and the legal description

Grantors and grantees must be labeled with those words so the clerk can index them. A street address is never accepted as a legal description. Documents signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, certified copies and papers executed outside the United States are exempt from the format rules, and a rejected document comes back with the reason written down.

sections.h2: Can Newton County documents be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, through an agreement with iCounty Technologies, LLC. The recorder's eRecord page names Dave Mudd and Lisa Norris at (816) 295-1540 as the contacts who set up that agreement. The office lists same day recording, payment by ACH and quick correction of a rejected document among the reasons to use it.

A rejected electronic filing can be corrected and sent again without a courier run. Electronic recording rests on RSMo 59.563, which lets a recorder set an electronic format but does not force any recorder to offer one.

sections.h2: What is Deed Watch and why would a Newton County owner sign up?
sections.html:
Deed Watch is a free property fraud alert. You visit DeedWatch.com, pick Newton County, Missouri, enter and confirm an email address, then add your search criteria, such as your name or parcel. The recorder's page describes it as a free service for catching recording activity on your property.

Owners of a vacant, inherited or rented Newton County house benefit most, since nobody is at the property to notice a forged deed or a lien filed against it. The recorder also posts instructions on how to flag suspicious recording activity.

sections.h2: What is Newton County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Newton County lies in the southwest corner of Missouri, is part of the Joplin metropolitan area, and has its seat in Neosho. The county was organized in 1838 and named for John Newton, a Revolutionary War hero. It covers about 625 square miles of land, and the 2020 census counted 58,648 residents. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 62,263, a gain of 6.1 percent since the April 2020 base.

Cities include Neosho, Seneca, Granby, Diamond and Fairview, and a corner of Joplin extends into the county from the north. School districts that cover Newton County addresses include Neosho R-V, East Newton County R-VI, Diamond R-IV and Seneca R-VII. The George Washington Carver National Monument is also inside the county.

sections.h2: What should I ask the recorder about a title problem on a Newton County house?
sections.html:
Nothing from this counter can clear a title. The recorder is the place to confirm that a deed of trust has a recorded release, that a plat or survey for the parcel is on file, and that a tax lien has been filed or released. The format page adds that releases and assignments must cite the book and page of the paper they refer to.

For anything beyond that, such as who holds a valid claim, bring in a title company or attorney. Sellers dealing with an inherited or tenant-occupied house often start with a title search to learn which recorded papers need a release before a buyer can close. Newton County also runs a delinquent tax sale each August, so a parcel with unpaid taxes can carry an extra recorded history.

sections.h2: Which Newton County offices matter besides the recorder?
sections.html:
Several county offices share the same courthouse, so one trip can cover them all. Ask each for current figures.

  • Assessor Cheryle Perkins, Suite 205, (417) 451-8228, places the value on real and personal property for tax purposes and keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30.
  • Collector Jessica Crawford, Suite 203, (417) 451-8217, issues tax bills and runs the delinquent tax sale on the fourth Monday of August.
  • County Clerk Tami Owens, (417) 451-8221, is the person to ask where a valuation appeal gets filed. The county lists its Board of Equalization among boards appointed by the commission.

The collector's page states that a tax obligation is fixed on January 1 and the law gives no pro-rating, and that the current owner is responsible for taxes due. Ask the title company how the year's bill is split on the closing statement, and ask the collector what is still unpaid before you sign. Bills are mailed November 1 and turn delinquent after midnight on December 31.

faqs.q: Does Newton County charge a transfer tax when a deed is recorded?
faqs.a: The county fee page lists no transfer tax line, only recording charges such as $26 for page one of a standard document. Ask your closing agent whether anything else is owed on your sale.

faqs.q: What time must I deliver a deed to Neosho to have it recorded the same day?
faqs.a: Bring it before 3:30 pm. The recorder is staffed until 4:30 pm, but recordings are accepted only until 3:30, and later papers are recorded the next business day in the order they arrived.

faqs.q: Can the Newton County recorder tell me who owns a house at a street address?
faqs.a: The recorder's site points to a name, legal description or recording reference as the way into the records, and staff cannot give legal advice. For a parcel by address, the assessor in Suite 205 at (417) 451-8228 is the better first call.

faqs.q: How can I send documents to the Newton County recorder without driving to Neosho?
faqs.a: You can mail them to P.O. Box 604 or use electronic recording through iCounty Technologies at (816) 295-1540. The office keeps up to $10 of any overpayment, so include enough to cover the fee.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed breaks the format rules?
faqs.a: The recorder can reject it and must return it with the reason. It can also be recorded for the $25 nonstandard surcharge on top of the normal page fees.
